passages.text: D.9-4 3 Details of this Opportunity 3.1 Scope As described in Section 2, HTMPO has been exploring the HWO mission architecture trade space, following the recommendation of Astro2020. The focus of HWO-ICA is to enable broader/deeper exploration of the instrument trade space, with the goal of better understanding of the range of possible HWO instruments, their relative scientific returns, and their engineering and technology challenges including accommodation. HTMPO is interested in understanding if the suite of candidate instruments studied thus far (see Section 2) can be improved (e.g., by combining certain instrument capabilities in different ways and/or simplifying certain candidate instruments), what instruments could be considered for the additional bay that has thus far remained empty, and any other innovative ideas that the community may have. This program element therefore solicits instrument concept assessments that respond to the broad science goals of HWO, including: the search for life on Earth-like planets around nearby Sun-like stars; measuring the hidden drivers of galaxy growth and evolution; and studying the origin and evolution of elements in the universe. Additionally, this program element solicits instrument concept assessments that may also address areas of planetary science. See Section 3.8 for additional resources on HWO science cases. The candidate instrument capabilities listed below are within the scope of this opportunity. Other instrument capabilities not listed here may be within the scope, if the proposal convincingly demonstrates sufficient traceability to HWO science goals. • Coronagraphy (*see note below): - Near-IR coronagraphic imaging and spectroscopy - Near-UV coronagraphic imaging • Spectroscopy: - UV / visible integral field spectroscopy - UV / visible multi-object spectroscopy • Imaging: - High-resolution near-UV / visible / near-IR imaging - Visible wavelength high-precision astrometry - Observatory guiding and wavefront sensing *Note that visible coronagraphic imaging and spectroscopy are excluded from this opportunity, as the visible coronagraph is being studied as directed work within HTMPO. Proposals may address near-IR / near-UV coronagraphy as a stand-alone instrument or as an additional channel within the visible coronagraph. HWO is currently in the pre-formulation phase, thus this opportunity does not solicit proposals to develop flight hardware or support tools/systems (e.g., ground support equipment, software). Proposers should note that HWO-ICA awards do not imply inclusion in future HWO instrument requirements or designs, nor involvement in future HWO mission development; decisions regarding HWO flight instruments will be made by NASA at a later date.

NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) Instrument Concept Assessments (HWO-ICA) program solicits proposals to support maturation of the HWO mission concept (see Section 2 for an overview of the HWO mission concept). The objective of HWO-ICA is to expand and deepen exploration of the HWO instrument trade space by developing and/or analyzing innovative instrument concepts and their scientific opportunity and performance, engineering feasibility and footprint, technology maturity and gaps, and associated risks (see Section 3.1 for scope details). This program is intended to support the ongoing pre-formulation activities being conducted by the HWO Technology Maturation Project Office (HTMPO); the scope, deliverables, and timelines of HWO-ICA activities are therefore aligned to HTMPO’s concurrent mission concept maturation activities (see Section 4). This opportunity does not support development of flight hardware or support tools/systems and does not imply participation in future HWO mission development (see Section 3.1).

Only U.S. organizations are eligible to submit proposals under this opportunity; n on-U.S. individuals may participate as unfunded Collaborators (see Section 3.6). In addition, U.S. -based individuals may propose for support of their participation in parallel non- U.S. opportunities (see Section 3.2.2). Awards made through this program element will be funded via contracts or Interagency Agreements (see Section 3.7).

[Amended September 3, 2026] - The only allowable funded personnel on a Category 2 proposal is the U.S.- based PI, therefore only the PI Biographical Sketch can be provided (unfunded U.S.-based individuals involved in the proposed work may be included as Collaborators)

passages.text: Molecular Imaging of Inflammation in Cancer (R01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

The purpose of this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is to invite research grant applications (R01) for the development and use of current and emerging molecular imaging methods to gain fundamental insights into cancer inflammation in vivo. The motivation for this initiative is that much of current imaging research into the role of inflammation in cancer is largely based on in vitro and ex vivo methods with limited utilization of imaging approaches that could lead to significant new insights relevant to dynamic cancer and inflammation interactions. Utilization of molecular imaging probes in pre-clinical and clinical investigations for precise temporal resolution at the molecular and cellular level are valuable approaches for identification and characterization of in vivo inflammatory cellular physiology in cancers and of molecular changes in response to treatment. This FOA encourages applications that focus on developing integrated imaging approaches to interrogate the role of inflammation in cancer through strong cross-field collaboration between cancer basic science researchers and imaging scientists. These collaborations are expected to advance science and understanding of cancer inflammation interactions.

Other Eligible Applicants include the following: Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian Serving Institutions; Asian American Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institutions (AANAPISISs); Eligible Agencies of the Federal Government; Faith-based or Community-based Organizations; Hispanic-serving Institutions; Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs); Indian/Native American Tribal Governments (Other than Federally Recognized); Non-domestic (non-U.S.) Entities (Foreign Organizations); Regional Organizations; Tribally Controlled Colleges and Universities (TCCUs) ; U.S. Territory or Possession; Non-domestic (non-U.S.) Entities (Foreign Organizations) are not eligible to apply. Non-domestic (non-U.S.) components of U.S. Organizations are not eligible to apply.

passages.text: Coordinating Center for National Resource Network for the Study of Human Auditory and Vestibular Disorders

The National Institutes on Deafness and other Communication Disorders (NIDCD) seeks to advance its mission by publishing a Notice of Funding Opportunity to solicit applications for a Coordinating Center for the National Human Ear Resource Network. The National Human Ear Resource Network is a critical national technological resource for auditory and vestibular researchers who use human inner and middle ear tissues for a range of basic and clinical studies. The Network serves as a nucleus for expanding the use of human temporal bones in the research community and facilitates communication and collaboration between laboratories that utilize human temporal bones in their research. It is anticipated that the Network Coordinating Center will, among other duties, coordinate and chair regular meetings with Network laboratories, work closely with NIDCD staff to disseminate to the scientific and clinical communities information regarding Network activities and facilitate communication and collaboration within the Network and with laboratories across the United States.
